failure_patterns.pattern: rule_wrong: The instruction to retain conventional initials encouraged an unnecessary middle initial where the expected answer used the shorter unambiguous name.

rejected_edits.content: When choosing a name form, distinguish the identifying name from generic type words supplied by the clue and from optional initials, suffixes, industry or type labels, and extra specificity found in a source title. Prefer the shortest common form that unambiguously fills the requested slot and matches the clue's granularity; omit generic labels when the clue already supplies that type. Retain conventional initials that form part of the common identifying name, but include other middle initials or suffixes only when needed to distinguish the entity or explicitly requested. Do not expand a generic term into a specific event name unless the clue asks for that specificity.
rejected_edits.target: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name; omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.

rejected_edits.content: For a bare comma- or ampersand-separated list of people, consider whether context clearly points to their shared country or jurisdiction rather than their relationship or category. If the named figures are distinctly associated with the same country, give that country; do not substitute a relationship such as “siblings” or a category such as “monarchs.” If no unique shared geographic relation is supported, do not infer one.
rejected_edits.target: When a prompt consists only of a list of character names or roles, use context to identify their shared work or program if that is the implied target. Return the work or program, not the performers, unless the prompt asks for the cast.

rejected_edits.content: When a clue quotes or describes a spoonerism, reverse the transposed sounds to identify the intended phrase. Give that corrected phrase when it is the clue's target, rather than the speaker or the spoonerism itself, unless the prompt explicitly asks for the speaker or the linguistic device.
